reason: Ship the previously agreed low-resource local-LLM capability as a mature-OSS-first product path: low-spec hardware must not be categorically restricted to small models. Yance may use upstream quantization, CPU/GPU hybrid offload, device-aware execution and layer/expert streaming from admitted OSS runtimes, while Yance itself remains only a thin lifecycle/planning/product adapter and never becomes an inference engine, quantizer, tensor scheduler or expert scheduler. Native Windows P0 execution admits the existing Ollama seam plus pinned llama.cpp; KTransformers is admitted only as WSL/user-managed MoE capability while native Windows remains upstream-deprecated, and AirLLM is admitted only as an extreme/background low-VRAM lane whose usability must be proven by measured benchmark evidence. Large upstream source/runtime archives and model weights are local-artifact inputs supplied on the user's machine and are never downloaded through the ChatGPT/GitHub connector path.

digestCanonicalization.pathNormalization: Require exact repository-relative normalized paths, remove duplicates, then sort with JavaScript default Array.prototype.sort().
digestCanonicalization.canonicalText: Join the normalized sorted unique path list with LF and append exactly one trailing LF before hashing.

expectedFailures: Current main has no adaptive local-runtime planner that distinguishes interactive, usable, background, extreme and incompatible execution from measured machine/runtime evidence.
Current isolated execution and execution-spec seams accept Ollama or credentialed cloud providers only; pinned llama.cpp, KTransformers WSL and AirLLM background lanes are not admitted.
Current ModelRuntimeAuthority treats provider === ollama as the only local model identity, so additional loopback local runtimes would be projected incorrectly.
Current Ollama lifecycle has discovery, stream, unload and delete but no governed pull/progress/cancel path, and current product surfaces have no downloadable adaptive local-model catalog.
Current product has no fail-closed local artifact materialization contract that verifies pinned upstream source/runtime assets supplied from the user's local machine.
Current product does not prove that low VRAM alone must not cap a machine to only small models when upstream hybrid/offload/streaming execution can satisfy a measured task SLA.

productContract.classificationRule: Classification must be based on runtime provenance plus measured or directly probed CPU/RAM/device/disk/throughput evidence. VRAM size or parameter count alone may not categorically forbid a larger model.

reviewedCandidates.name: Ollama
reviewedCandidates.reason: Existing main already discovers, executes, unloads and deletes Ollama models. Extend the upstream pull lifecycle instead of inventing a downloader or inference engine.

reviewedCandidates.name: llama.cpp
reviewedCandidates.reason: Mature upstream provides quantization, CPU/GPU hybrid inference for models larger than VRAM, OpenAI-compatible server mode, and official Windows CPU/CUDA/Vulkan artifacts. This is the primary new native-Windows low-resource runtime.

reviewedCandidates.name: KTransformers
reviewedCandidates.reason: Mature CPU/GPU heterogeneous MoE execution is useful for very large models, but upstream currently documents native Windows as temporarily deprecated and recommends WSL. V1 may expose only a truthful WSL/user-managed lane.

reviewedCandidates.name: AirLLM
reviewedCandidates.reason: Layer-streaming can make very large models runnable at very low VRAM, but disk I/O can dominate latency. V1 may admit it only as extreme/background until measured evidence proves a stronger class on the actual machine.

retireOrAvoid: Do not write or fork a Yance inference kernel, quantizer, GGUF engine, tensor scheduler, KV-cache engine, MoE expert scheduler or layer streamer.
Do not duplicate LiteLLM provider selection, retry, fallback or cooldown authority.
Do not replace upstream llama.cpp/KTransformers/AirLLM algorithms with Yance reimplementations; adapters may only materialize, launch, probe, transport, classify evidence and expose lifecycle state.
Do not claim KTransformers native Windows support while upstream documents that path as temporarily deprecated.
Do not label AirLLM extreme execution interactive solely because a model can load or generate one token.

manifestMustPin: official artifact filename or source archive identity

negativeProofs: No local runtime service present: formal cloud Model Brain remains available and no local prerequisite is introduced.
llama.cpp local server without API key is accepted only on a loopback endpoint; cloud OpenAI-compatible endpoints still require credentials.
A machine with small VRAM can still receive a larger-model hybrid/background/extreme recommendation when direct runtime/benchmark evidence supports it.
A model that merely loads but misses measured latency/throughput/resource thresholds is not labeled interactive.
KTransformers is not presented as native Windows in V1.
AirLLM cannot become formal quick_reply/deep_reply/director authority.
No large binary/model artifact becomes a Git-tracked change in the implementation branch.
